history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTED: the temple is at Kayavarohan (also called Karvan), Dabhoi taluka, Vadodara district, about 24-30 km from Vadodara city - not in Vadodara town. An ancient mahatirtha regarded as the birthplace of Lakulisha, the 28th incarnation of Shiva and founder-figure of the Pashupata sect; it is one of the 68 Shiva teerthas of the Shiva Purana and is called the 'Kashi of Gujarat'. The formless, unique lingam is a meditating yogi in shambhavi mudra holding a parchment and a citron (matulinga), carved in black stone; the complex also has an underground meditation cave. Legend says the luminous jyotirlinga merged with the other twelve jyotirlingas and disappeared during Mahmud of Ghazni's invasion. The murti now installed was unearthed in nearby fields in the 19th century; 20th-century saint Swami Kripalvanandji had the present temple built around it (sources cite 1955 and 1974 - CONFLICT). Coordinates are approximate (village-level geocode). NOTE: one low-quality source claims this is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas - this is FALSE; Kayavarohan is not among them.

name: Kayavarohan Temple
town_description: Kayavarohan (Karvan) is a village in Dabhoi taluka of Vadodara district, Gujarat, set amid farmland about 25-30 km from Vadodara city. It is an ancient pilgrimage town believed to have existed through all four yugas, and was in Vedic times a centre of learning with Vedic universities and yajna shalas. Archaeological finds from the area include 2nd-century sculptures and relics.

travel.railway: Kayavarohan and Vadodara are the nearest railheads
travel.road: On NH 8, about 6-7 km from Por and ~24-30 km south of Vadodara; buses available from Por bus stand

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Maha Shivratri for the main festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opens ~5:00 AM, closes late evening (single weak source - verify). Last stretch of the road is rural with no street lights - daytime visits advised. Accommodation and food available at the site's yoga centre/ashram (verify). Dress modestly; remove shoes in temple areas.
